cnn.title: COP31 in Turkey ends without a deal
cnn.desc:
The UN climate summit in Turkey collapses after the final draft text makes no direct mention of fossil fuels, which proved unacceptable to the European Union and Pacific island countries. Poorer governments had also objected to the lack of clear financial commitments to help them adapt to climate change.
Also: Russia hits Ukrainian energy facilities, straining power supplies and causing widespread power cuts. There's been a suspected drone attack on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi in Libya. In football, the new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino suffers a brutal debut as Liverpool cruise to a 4–0 win. Britain is starting the world's largest trial of artificial intelligence to help breast cancer screening. Israel’s opposition leader says arson attacks in the West Bank amount to Jewish terrorism. The Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari has died aged 89.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Global Story: AI can imitate a human. But can it think like one?
cnn.desc: For decades, computer scientists have been trying to figure out whether computers can think. But with the advent of highly sophisticated chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT…might we finally have our answer? This week we’re introducing The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today. We constantly hear stories about artificial intelligence, but most of them are about where AI is going; in this five-episode series we’re looking at where it came from. Beginning with computer scientist Alan Turing’s famous Turing test in 1950, the quest to verify the existence of machine intelligence has taken on many forms – from the rudimentary chatbots of the 1960s, to the 1997 defeat of a chess grand master by a computer, to IBM Watson’s stint on Jeopardy in the 2010s. But large language models have rendered old methods of measuring machine intelligence obsolete. So how smart is AI, anyway? And will it ever be smarter than us? Tristan Redman and Asma Khalid are joined by Thomas Germain, BBC technology columnist and host of the BBC podcast The Interface. The Global Story brings clarity to politics, business and foreign policy in a time of connection and disruption. For more episodes, just search 'The Global Story' wherever you get your BBC Podcasts.

cnn.title: Deadlock at UN climate summit in Turkey
cnn.desc:
The COP31 summit has gone into a second day of overtime after talks were suspended for the night. There is no agreement in sight with the European Union and Pacific Island nations threatening to walk away without agreeing to a deal because the draft text makes no mention of reducing global demand for fossil fuels. Also: Croatians take to the streets over the death in hospital of a psychiatric patient who was beaten and smothered. We hear from British endurance athlete Lewis Pugh who swam through the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the environmental cost of the war between the US and Iran. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah visits India to try to secure much needed financial aid following devastating floods in the Himalayan nation. And has a maths problem that has puzzled humans for 167 years finally been solved?The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: The Happy Pod: The 'amazing’ device that controls Tourette's
cnn.desc: We meet 17-year-old Mylo who's taken part in a trial of the watch-like device that suppresses his Tourette's tics. He can even now go to the cinema without fear of causing a disturbance by constantly moving or clearing his throat. Also: the chef in Japan who's known poverty and illness and now offers free meals to people in the position he was once in; the NASA spacecraft, Voyager One, that's become the first human-made object to reach a point one light day from Earth; the surf school in Senegal that's trying to turn its pupils into world champions; and the children with autism and ADHD who've been helped by alpacas. Image: 17-year-old Mylo wearing the device. Credit: BBC News.Our weekly collection of inspiring, uplifting and happy news from around the world.Presenter:  Holly Gibbs. Music composed by Iona Hampson

cnn.title: Man found guilty of starting deadly LA wildfire
cnn.desc:
Jonathan Rinderknecht is found guilty of starting the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles, which displaced thousands of people and became one of the most destructive fires in the city’s history. Also: Donald Trump describes his relationship with the leaders of Russia and China as “fantastic”, after meeting with them in Shenzhen. The US president also threatens a ban on American firms building AI data centres overseas, saying they must stay in the US. Russian drones continue to attack Ukraine, with Poland caught in the crossfire. Students in more than 20 European countries protest over education, climate change and military conscription. Cyber security experts in the UK conduct a highly secretive operation to protect its fridges and freezers. Cincinnati Zoo announces the death of the beloved hippo, Fiona. cnn.desc:
UK and EU agree new deal covering food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions. European Commission President, Ursula von der Leyen, said it marked a "turning point" in relations. Also: BBC speaks to people inside the besieged city of Taiz in Yemen. Why the Malaysian government wants to settle 10,000 Rohingyas in Turkey. A group of eight European and developing countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey says a global call to "accelerate the phase-out of fossil fuels" must be restored to the final agreement. Several people are killed and more than a dozen are injured in Ukraine's capital Kyiv, after Russia fires 100 missiles and 400 drones at the city. cnn.title: Abusers convicted in Joanne Young case echoing Pelicot
cnn.desc:
In the first trial of its kind in England, four men have been convicted of raping and sexually abusing a British woman, in a harrowing case that bears similarities to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France. Like Pelicot, Joanne Young chose to allow her name to be made public, after discovering that her then-husband had advertised her online to strangers for sex, repeatedly drugged her and raped her. British police sought the expertise of French investigators on the Pelicot case to assist them in bringing Young's former husband and her other abusers to justice.Also: AI tech giant Anthropic becomes one of the world's most valuable public companies after its stock market debut. Meanwhile Meta says it is ''re-evaluating'' its 2030 climate goals as the demand for AI data centres drives up emissions. A spacecraft that has been on an eight year journey through outer space is set to enter orbit around Mercury. We hear the Ukrainian view on the face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035. We meet the winner of the International Children's Peace Prize, 17-year-old Colombian climate activist Francisco Vera Manzanares. And who are the candidates challenging Fifa President Gianni Infantino for the top job in world football? The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: UN court says Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingyas
cnn.desc:

The ICJ rejected Myanmar’s argument that it had responded to insurgent attacks.Also: the presidents of China, the US and Russia stress the importance of stable energy flows, UN reform and the prevention of nuclear proliferation at a trilateral summit, internet access is cut in South Korean exam halls, amid fears of cheating. cnn.title: BBC reports from Ukraine's undergound frontier
cnn.desc:
We go inside the old Soviet-era gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the tunnels where this subterranean battle is taking place. Also: the AI giant Anthropic is set to raise more than 80 billion dollars in its initial public offering, breaking a record set by SpaceX. President Trump pushes back against global regulation of ''Super Intelligence'' - or AI - at the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of his meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. The US defence secretary Pete Hegseth signs a military cooperation deal with America's former foe Venezuela. Democrats in the US House of Representatives nominate Hakeem Jeffries as first African American Speaker. A new study suggests a pill that mimics Viagra can slow cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third. Rare footage from Brazil shows about 20 Indigenous men and boys emerging from their self-imposed isolation deep in the Amazon rainforest. And a painting by Vincent Van Gogh sells at auction in New York for over 190 million dollars - a record for work by the artist. cnn.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
cnn.desc:
President Trump was greeted by President Xi Jinping at the airport as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting on Thursday between the pair and the Russian president. In a highly choreographed moment, Trump and Xi shook hands on the tarmac. Later the US leader met Mr Putin ahead of a gala dinner. Also: Thousands of people in Haiti have marched in the capital in support of troops from El Salvador, who've been deployed to confront the island's powerful criminal gangs. The Democrats have taken Alaska from the Republicans in the final senate race of the US midterms, nearly three weeks after election day. We hear from a former child refugee from South Sudan, who has walked the entire length of the UK to draw attention to the war in Sudan. And - after more than 13 years, GTA 6 - the latest instalment of the multi billion dollar video game franchise is released amid huge fanfare and expectation.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Nvidia rules out return for disgraced boss
cnn.desc:
Jensen Huang fails in his bid to be re-hired as CEO of Nvidia after a scandal over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating whether the company misled investors. Nvidia has meanwhile reported a doubling of revenues during his last quarter in charge.Also: President Donald Trump is attending a regional economic summit in China, a day ahead of a historic meeting with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, and the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, in the city of Shenzhen. The US has lost its measles-free status and infections are continuing to spread. Researchers have been learning more about humpback whales by using drones to collect their snot. We have a report from the West Bank after a 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot dead by armed settlers in Jericho. New research has found that genes inherited from Neanderthals can reduce the risk of schizophrenia. A Georgia O'Keefe painting that was hidden in a cupboard for years has sold at auction for 4.8 million dollars. And the spacecraft Voyager 1 will clock up a milestone - reaching a distance of one light day from earth.The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. cnn.title: Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
cnn.desc:
This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week.
The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home?
